answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by funneling new identities through a verified inlet where each must pass a falcon-grade proof-of-personhood. Cloning fails because every opal-keyed credential is bound to one device and one stake. Peers downgrade any twin that reuses a credential, slashing its deposit instantly. Because each forged identity must repay the full entry cost, mass spawning becomes an unprofitable drain on the attacker.
